Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. Nick Kelly and Henry Nicholls are out to open for New Zealand. Shoriful Islam will be bowling the first over of this chase.
... The Run Chase ...

New Zealand have done just enough - New Zealand’s bowling attack enjoyed a dream start behind the efforts of Will O'Rourke and Nathan Smith, with Will particularly effective in extracting swing to leave the hosts reeling early on. However, Bangladesh seized control during the middle overs, neutralizing the Kiwi spinners to steer the innings back on track. While Lister and Lennox managed to claim two wickets apiece, they proved expensive, and the likes of Abbas and Smith struggled to make a lasting impression as the partnership grew. Ultimately, Will O'Rourke remained the standout performer, finishing with a deserved three-wicket haul, and a disciplined performance in the final five overs shifted the momentum back toward the visitors. While New Zealand will back their chances following that late surge, the hosts will feel they have posted a competitive total well within their capability to defend. Stay tuned.

Shanto leads the chart - Despite a precarious start that saw Bangladesh reeling at 9/2 after just three overs, a magnificent century from Najmul Hossain Shanto anchored a brilliant recovery. Walking into the teeth of a fierce spell from Will O'Rourke, who was finding immense success with the new ball, Shanto partnered with Litton Das to stabilize the innings. The duo’s aggressive yet calculated 160-run stand off just 178 deliveries effectively shifted the momentum and neutralized the early threat. While Towhid Hridoy and Mehidy Hasan Miraz contributed useful cameos to keep the scoreboard ticking, the finishing kick lacked its usual sting. Bangladesh left some runs on the table by managing only 34 runs and losing three wickets in the final five overs, concluding an otherwise dominant outing with a slightly muted flourish.

PITCH REPORT - HD Ackerman observes that while batting in Dhaka was challenging, the pitch in Chattogram presents a sensational opportunity for runs. He notes a healthy covering of grass and underlying moisture that should keep the cracks from widening, while describing the playing area as an upside-down dinner plate with an outfield that slopes away from the pitch. Given the boundary dimensions, 60m and 65m on the square and 76m straight, Ackerman predicts a high count of boundaries despite New Zealand's lack of sixes in the opening matches and identifies chasing as the optimal strategy for the day.

Bangladesh captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz - Miraz says he was looking to bat first, citing his comfort with the conditions and the pitch's high quality. Miraz stresses that the top order must take responsibility as they did in the previous game and build solid partnerships to set a competitive total. Miraz informs that Mustafizur Rahman and Tanvir Islam are replacing Taskin Ahmed and Rishad Hossain.

New Zealand captain Tom Latham - Latham says that statistics from both day games and previous matches at the venue suggest chasing is the easier path. Tom adds that the importance of adapting quickly to the surface, which he observes played significantly differently for Bangladesh in the prior match, compared to the first wicket. Latham aims to gather crucial information about the pitch's behavior to guide his team's approach during the chase, encouraging his players to compete with freedom. Latham adds that Ben Lister joins the starting XI to replace Blair Tickner, who is sidelined with a niggle.

Where the series could be decided - The contest is likely to hinge on the battle in the middle overs. Whichever side manages to rotate strike effectively while containing the opposition’s scoring will gain a decisive edge. Additionally, not losing wickets in a cluster could ultimately separate the two teams. In a finely poised series, it may just come down to who executes better when it matters most. Toss and team news in a bit.

Bangladesh’s game plan - Bangladesh, buoyed by their comeback win, will aim to carry forward the confidence and aggression that defined their second ODI performance. Their batting unit showed resilience and intent, something they must replicate under the pressure of a series decider. The bowlers, especially the spinners, played a crucial role in disrupting New Zealand’s rhythm, and they will once again be central to Bangladesh’s chances. To clinch the series, Bangladesh must stay fearless but disciplined, ensuring they capitalize on key moments without letting the game drift.

New Zealand’s approach - New Zealand will look to return to the structured, clinical brand of cricket that earned them victory in the first ODI. Their strength lies in adaptability, building solid partnerships at the top and finishing strongly with power hitters down the order. The bowling unit, particularly in the middle overs, will need to regain control and apply pressure through tight lines and smart field placements. For New Zealand, minimizing lapses and maintaining consistency across all phases of the game will be key to sealing the series.

Series on the line - Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in. The stage is perfectly set for a thrilling decider as New Zealand and Bangladesh head into the third ODI with the series locked at 1-1. New Zealand drew first blood with a convincing win in the opener, showcasing their balance and discipline, while Bangladesh roared back in the second game with a spirited performance that underlined their growing confidence in the format. With momentum shifting and both teams having tasted success, the final clash promises high stakes, pressure moments, and a definitive answer to who holds their nerve better.

Decider awaits in Chattogram - The stage now shifts to the Bir Shrestha Shahid Flight Lieutenant Motiur Rahman Cricket Stadium for the all-important third ODI, with the series beautifully poised at 1-1 between Bangladesh and New Zealand. What started with New Zealand's clinical win in the opener has now turned into a proper contest, thanks to Bangladesh's emphatic response in the second game. With everything to play for, this decider has all the ingredients of a gripping finale. Heroes in every chapter - New Zealand drew first blood with a composed performance, where Dean Foxcroft's all-round brilliance and solid contributions from Henry Nicholls and Will Young powered them to a defendable total. But Bangladesh flipped the script in style in the second ODI, led by a fiery spell from Nahid Rana, whose five-wicket haul dismantled the Kiwi lineup. With the bat, Tanzid Hasan continued his rich vein of form, while Najmul Hossain Shanto and Tawhid Hridoy ensured there were no late hiccups in the chase. Two games, two different stories and now, one final chapter. Confidence rising - Back on home soil, Bangladesh look like a side growing in belief. Their recent series win over Pakistan, combined with the way they bounced back here, speaks volumes about their resilience. The top order, led by Tanzid, has been consistent, while players like Litton Das and Soumya Sarkar add depth and experience. With the ball, the pace of Nahid Rana alongside Taskin Ahmed and the control of Rishad Hossain gives them a well-rounded attack suited to these conditions. System over stars - Despite missing several first-choice players, New Zealand have once again shown the strength of their system. Players like Foxcroft have stepped up, while Nick Kelly's fighting 83 in the last game highlighted their batting depth. The likes of Blair Tickner and Nathan Smith have been key with the ball, and the Kiwis will back their discipline to bounce back. More importantly, they have a bigger incentive, a chance to make it five consecutive ODI series wins since the 2025 Champions Trophy. Pitch and pressure - Chattogram offers a slightly different test compared to Dhaka, a surface that can be slower but generally provides a fair contest. The average first innings score here hovers around 220-230, and interestingly, chasing sides have had more success, winning 19 out of 31 ODIs at this venue. That brings both tactics and temperament into play. Beyond this match, crucial ODI Super League points are at stake, with Bangladesh aiming to strengthen their push for direct qualification to the 2027 World Cup, while New Zealand look to continue their dominant run in bilateral series. Team form (Last 5 completed ODIs, recent first) - BAN - WLWLW | NZ - LWWWL. The final act - Two teams, contrasting journeys, but now level on the scoreboard. Bangladesh have the momentum and home advantage, while New Zealand have the composure and winning habit. It all comes down to who handles the pressure better on the day because in a decider like this, it's not just about skill, it's about nerve.
